_meta.source: toy experiment (toy model trained for this explainer, src/image_ebt.py + src/image_export.py)
_meta.note: Tiny conv EBT vs same-size one-shot denoiser and same-size diffusion (DDIM) denoiser on a 5000-image CIFAR-10 subset at 32x32 RGB, trained for a few minutes on one CPU core each. NOT the paper's result: the paper's image numbers are Table 4 / Fig 10 / Fig 12 (COCO 2014 128x128, DiT-L sized models, 100k steps). Images come from the Hugging Face datasets-server JPEG previews of uoft-cs/cifar10 (quality ~75), so 'clean' means the decoded JPEG.
_meta.psnr_definition: PSNR = 10*log10(255^2 / MSE), MSE on 0..255 pixels averaged over all eval pixels (this matches how paper Table 4 PSNR and MSE relate). psnr_mean_per_image also given.
_meta.verdict: In this toy, the baselines win on PSNR: one-shot FF and few-step DDIM beat the EBT at sigma=0.1 and sigma=0.2, and the gap grows if FF gets the same wall-clock instead of the same number of steps. What the toy does show: (1) the noise-start EBT's quality rises with thinking steps and then plateaus without collapsing (the x-start EBT peaks at 2-4 steps and then drifts down slowly), while the toy diffusion model degrades with long chains and collapses at OOD noise; (2) OOD inputs get higher energy (mean energy after 16 steps 153 at sigma=0.1 vs 389 at sigma=0.2); (3) paper-style recursion helps at OOD noise for both families; the best EBT number at sigma=0.2 (x-start, recursive x3, 19.7 dB) beats step-matched FF and direct DDIM but not recursive DDIM (20.4 dB); (4) Best-of-4 by lowest energy adds only 0.12 dB at 2 steps (all starts fall into the same bowl), but it always beats picking the highest-energy sample. The paper's real result (EBT beats DiT, Table 4 / Fig 12) is at far larger scale.
caveats: Training steps (batch 32): EBT noise-start 189, EBT x-start 113 (stopped by the ~8 minute cap), FF 189 and diffusion 189 (step-matched to the EBT), FF wall-clock-matched 581.
The CPU was shared with other jobs (load 8-20 on 4 cores), so wall-clock numbers are noisy.
Models are tiny (about 69k parameters) and far from converged; all numbers are toy demonstrations.
diff_best picks the best K on the eval set, which flatters the diffusion baseline.
Recursive x3 follows paper App. D.3 in spirit; the exact recursion details are our interpretation.
EBT x-start starts from the noisy observation; it peaks after 2-4 steps and then slowly gets worse, so more steps are not always better for that variant.
Eval set: first 300 CIFAR-10 test images (one fixed noise draw per sigma).

noise.schedule: DDPM linear beta from 1e-4 to 2e-2 over T=1000 steps (paper Sec 4.3, p.13)
noise.sigma_definition: sigma = fraction of the schedule; t = round(sigma*T); x_noisy = sqrt(abar_t)*y + sqrt(1-abar_t)*eps, abar_t = prod_{s=1..t}(1-beta_s)
noise.index_note: The paper does not state the index convention; DiT/guided-diffusion code indexes alphas_cumprod from 0, which would use abar after t+1 steps. The difference is tiny (see alpha_bar_if_0_indexed).

hparams.trunk: conv net, SiLU: conv3x3 24 @32px -> avgpool -> conv 48 @16px -> 2 residual conv 48 -> conv 24 -> nearest upsample + skip -> conv 24 -> conv3x3 to 3 channels

ebt.think: yhat_{i+1} = yhat_i - alpha * dE/dyhat_i, yhat_0 ~ N(0, I) (paper Alg. 1)
ebt.init_choice_reason: We start from pure noise, exactly like paper Algorithm 1, so every bit of the clean image has to come from descending the learned energy. Starting from x_noisy would also work for denoising but would hide that the energy landscape alone carries the prediction.
ebt.loss: MSE(yhat_N, y) at the last step, backprop through all steps (second order)
ebt.inference: deterministic gradient descent, same alpha, no noise, up to 32 steps

ff.output: clean image in one forward pass

ff_time.note: same FF model given the same WALL-CLOCK budget as the EBT (more optimizer steps)

diff.sampler: DDIM (eta=0) from t=sigma*T to 0 with K steps, x0 clipped to [-1,1]
diff.ood_note: At sigma=0.2 (t=200) the diffusion model also sees an unseen timestep input.

hparams.nfe_note: NFE counts network evaluations. One EBT step = one forward + one backward through the energy net (about 3x the FLOPs of a forward pass), the paper also counts it as one pass.
hparams.training_compute_note: Each EBT training step backpropagates through 2-3 gradient steps (second order); on the shared CPU it took about 2.6 s vs 0.8-1.0 s for an FF step (roughly 3x), see train_curves wall_seconds.

0.1.diff_note: DDIM from t=sigma*T down to 0 in K evenly spaced steps (NFE=K). K=t (one step per schedule step) is the natural full chain; diff_best is the best K on the eval set, an optimistic choice for the baseline.

energy_slice.what: ENERGY landscape (not the training loss): E(x, yhat) for ONE fixed noisy context x and the final trained weights, on a 2D plane through yhat-space (3072 dims). Origin = EBT step-16 prediction; axis u (columns) = direction to the start yhat0; axis v (rows) = direction to the true clean image (orthogonalized), so start, final prediction and truth all lie in the plane. Path = projection of the 16 gradient steps onto this plane. energy[i][j] is at (u[j], v[i]).

0.2.diff_note: DDIM from t=sigma*T down to 0 in K evenly spaced steps (NFE=K). K=t (one step per schedule step) is the natural full chain; diff_best is the best K on the eval set, an optimistic choice for the baseline.
0.2.recursive_note: Paper App. D.3: at OOD noise both models did best when applied 3 times recursively to their own output. Our reading: each application treats its input as noise level sigma=0.1 (t=100), the training level.

energy_slice.what: ENERGY landscape (not the training loss): E(x, yhat) for ONE fixed noisy context x and the final trained weights, on a 2D plane through yhat-space (3072 dims). Origin = EBT step-16 prediction; axis u (columns) = direction to the start yhat0; axis v (rows) = direction to the true clean image (orthogonalized), so start, final prediction and truth all lie in the plane. Path = projection of the 16 gradient steps onto this plane. energy[i][j] is at (u[j], v[i]).

findings: sigma=0.1: EBT (noise start) goes from 12.9 dB after 1 step to 21.2 dB after 4 and 21.6 dB at its best (13 steps); one-shot FF gets 23.2 dB, DDIM best 23.3 dB at 2 passes. The longest DDIM chain we ran (100 passes from t=100) gets 22.4 dB. FF trained for the same wall-clock as the EBT gets 24.4 dB.

sigma=0.2: EBT (noise start) goes from 11.7 dB after 1 step to 17.6 dB after 4 and 17.7 dB at its best (7 steps); one-shot FF gets 19.3 dB, DDIM best 18.9 dB at 3 passes. The longest DDIM chain we ran (100 passes from t=200) gets 5.3 dB. FF trained for the same wall-clock as the EBT gets 19.8 dB. EBT applied 3x recursively (4 steps each, 12 passes) gets 18.3 dB. DDIM applied 3x recursively gets up to 20.4 dB (6 passes).
